# Rosalind Penrose

## Overview

- **Age:** Forty-five  <sub>[v1 c19 P52](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0052), [v1 c19 P86](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0086), [v1 c23 P11](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0011)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c19 P52](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0052)</sub>
- **Status:** Married  <sub>[v1 c30 P31](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0031)</sub>
- **Origin:** St. Brendan's Island  <sub>[v1 c2 P24](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0024), [v1 c19 P52](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0052), [v1 c23 P23](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0023)</sub>
- **Titles:** Miss Rosalind  <sub>[v1 c19 P77](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0077), [v1 c19 P89](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0089)</sub>; Mrs. Stanhope  <sub>[v1 c28 P43](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0043), [v1 c30 P31](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0031)</sub>

## Appearance

Rosalind is a slender, remarkably tiny woman with a youthful face, rosy cheeks, sweet lips, large gentle brown eyes featuring tiny gold flecks, and dimples. She has lovely, thick, wavy snow-white hair styled in flattering puffs and coils. She frequently dresses in delicate cream muslin adorned with light-colored roses or vibrant deep red dresses accompanied by a gray silk shawl.

_Sources: [v1 c19 P77](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0077), [v1 c19 P89](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0089), [v1 c19 P97](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0097), [v1 c23 P5](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0005), [v1 c23 P6](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0006)_

## Personality

Rosalind is a charming, warm, and highly imaginative woman who retains a youthful spirit despite her years. She enjoys fantasy, pretending, and creating elaborate daydreams, often admitting that she could hardly survive without her imagination. Though sensitive, moody, and proud in her past, she possesses an adaptable, affectionate nature, a love for poetry, and a deep appreciation for the beauty of nature.

_Sources: [v1 c19 P54](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0054), [v1 c19 P86](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0086), [v1 c19 P92](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0092), [v1 c19 P97](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0097), [v1 c23 P11](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0011), [v1 c23 P19](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0019)_

## Goals

- To retain her youthful spirit and imagination throughout her life  <sub>[v1 c19 P62](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0062), [v1 c23 P11](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0011)</sub>

## History

Rosalind Penrose grew up at Echo Cottage, a picturesque red sandstone home in Middle Welby. At age twenty, she became engaged to Stephen Stanhope, but a foolish quarrel fueled by pride and moodiness broke the engagement, prompting Stephen to leave for the United States. Rosalind remained at Echo Cottage for twenty-five years as a spinster, passing her time with gardening, daydreams, and a succession of hired girls whom she invariably called Belinda. In her middle years, she formed a close bond of friendship with Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke, who frequently visited her secluded cottage. After Nell accidentally revealed to Stephen Stanhope that Rosalind remained unmarried, Stephen visited Echo Cottage to seek her forgiveness. The two reconciled, resulting in their marriage in the garden under the honeysuckle trellis. Following the wedding, Rosalind departed with her husband to reside in Boston, planning to return to Echo Cottage each summer.

_Sources: [v1 c19 P28](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0028), [v1 c19 P52](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0052), [v1 c19 P76](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0076), [v1 c23 P13](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0013), [v1 c23 P18](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0018), [v1 c28 P30](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0030), [v1 c28 P44](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0044), [v1 c29 P31](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0031)_

## Background by volume

- Born in St. Brendan's Island to parents who named her after her father's love of lavender
- Engaged at age twenty to Stephen Stanhope before a tragic misunderstanding separated them for twenty-five years  <sub>[v1 c23 P13](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0013), [v1 c23 P18](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0018)</sub>
- Lived for decades as a secluded spinster in Echo Cottage with a series of young hired girls named Belinda  <sub>[v1 c19 P52](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0052)</sub>

## Quotes

> I am not sure I object to disposing of the platter. However, twenty-five dollars is its value. The platter is extremely old.  <sub>[v1 c19 P61](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0061)</sub>

> I suppose the validity of your request for sympathy matches my own. Everything hinges on our perspective. Take a seat in this spot and describe yourself to me.  <sub>[v1 c19 P88](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0088)</sub>

> I suppose I might if you drop by to chat with me every now and then  <sub>[v1 c19 P90](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0090)</sub>

> Bear in mind, you Nell-girl, that you are to pay me a visit when you arrive in town, where I will lodge you in the most unoccupied spare-room bed I have for sleeping.  <sub>[v1 c19 P96](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0096)</sub>

> I am aware you will consider me terribly silly... I am silly . . . and I feel humiliated about it whenever I am caught, but only when I am caught.  <sub>[v1 c21 P53](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0053)</sub>
